review_notes: All five scores survive and match the primary refutation, which this dossier does not change. Trasen judicial +1/low: the only signal is the treatment-to-reduce-recidivism plank [S4]. There is no interpretive-method statement, so low is the right ceiling and the score stays out of alignment math. Trasen safety +1/high: I tested this as possibly overstated, since the dossier calls the treatment plank 'a stated priority, not a documented record' [S4]. High still rests on a record, 26 years of public defense and appeals [S1][S5], plus an explicit statement, and the same call was upheld in the primary. It also sits sensibly above Merfeld (SW5, +1/medium), whose formation is mixed prosecution/defense. Tse safety -1/medium: a 16-year prosecution formation including homicide [S4][S6]. Her campaign value 'Safety' (community accountability, 'holistic approaches') [S4] is too vague to pull the score toward 0, and the score is symmetric with Walls (SW5) and Rose-Akins (W1). Experience -1/medium for both holds: Trasen is a full-time ALJ with pro tem service; Tse runs on a '30-year career in trial courts' and pro tem service since 2021 [S1][S2][S4]. Citations check out in each candidate's own dossier. No basis uses the King County Democrats endorsement. Summary/highlight flags: Trasen's summary ends 'endorsed by the King County Democrats' as one of its two sentences, while Tse's summary has no endorsement. In a nonpartisan race where the dossier says party endorsements are not evidence, consider replacing it with her bar ratings or her full-time ALJ role, or giving both summaries parallel endorsement facts (Tse lists Gov. Locke, Justice Ireland and East Division judges [S5]). Otherwise the summaries, highlights and race_blurb are supported and neutral.
